items.english: "Well, abroad there are men who have gone at it on a larger scale and have even studied the language of monkeys."
notes: Speaker is not named in the text; reads as the host carrying on from his loud laugh at p129.

items.english: "If I ever get to learn English or something, I will try it myself, eh —"

notes: Speaker is not named in the text;reads as one of the group capping Nekohachi rather than the host.

items.english: "Wa ha, ha," two or three of them came out together.

"..." He felt quite as if his own stock in trade had been taken from him, and his spirits fell a little flat. Just to cover it, "They say on learned grounds that the monkey has turned into man, but in the story here the tiger has turned into a monkey, eh."
notes: o-kabu wo torareta is his patter for having his thunder stolen; kept as stock in trade to hold the yose sense.

items.english: "No, we are glad to have it in your animal mimicry too," the host answered.

"That aside," the man with the face like Tenjin-sama, whom he had till now thought a disagreeable fellow, asked him a good question this time. "I want to hear your motive for coming to do such things, eh."
notes: Kept Tenjin-sama as in the bible; the ne is the man's, not Nekohachi's na.

items.english: "Well, call it the first notion that started it."

data.say: Drafted the monkey English exchange and the turn to motives without polishing either side.
